proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(n\geq 1\), \(d\geq 2\), and \(0<\epsilon<1/2\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:separated\mbox{-}atom\mbox{-}lower}\) and \(\mathrm{thm:scalar\mbox{-}transfer\mbox{-}lower}\), there are constants \(c_{1,\epsilon}>0\) and \(c_{2,\epsilon}>0\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), for which
\[
 R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_{1,\epsilon}\min\!\left\{\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right\},
 \qquad
 R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq c_{2,\epsilon}\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
If \(r\geq c_1 a\) and \(r\geq c_2 b\) for nonnegative \(a,b,r\) and positive \(c_1,c_2\), then
\[
 r\geq \min\{c_1,c_2\}\max\{a,b\}.
\]
Applying this elementary implication and then \(\mathrm{def:benchmarks}\) gives
\[
 R_{n,d,\epsilon}\geq
 \min\{c_{1,\epsilon},c_{2,\epsilon}\}
 \max\!\left\{
   \min\!\left(1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right),
   \min\!\left(\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right)
 \right\}
 =c_\epsilon L_{n,d},
\]
after setting \(c_\epsilon=\min\{c_{1,\epsilon},c_{2,\epsilon}\}>0\).

For the upper bound, \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}}\) is, by \(\mathrm{thm:empirical\mbox{-}upper}\), a measurable \(\mathcal P([-1,1])\)-valued statistic.  It is therefore an admissible decision rule in the infimum defining \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\) in \(\mathrm{def:minimax\mbox{-}risk}\).  Hence
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 &\leq \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,\epsilon}}
 E_{P^n}\!\left[W_1(\widehat G_{\mathrm{emp}},G_P)^2\right] \\
 &\leq C_\epsilon\min\!\left(1,\frac dn\right)
 =C_\epsilon U_{n,d},
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the second inequality is \(\mathrm{thm:empirical\mbox{-}upper}\) and the equality is \(\mathrm{def:benchmarks}\).  All constants depend only on the fixed overlap constant \(\epsilon\), so both inequalities hold uniformly over the stated \(n\) and \(d\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Uniformly over \(n\geq1\) and \(d\geq2\), there are constants \(c_\epsilon>0\) and \(C_\epsilon<\infty\), depending only on \(\epsilon\), such that
\[
 c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d}.
\]
Thus the explicit lower benchmark characterizes the minimax squared-Wasserstein risk to within a factor of at most \(\log(ed)\) on the original unrestricted model class.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The lower inequality is the lower inequality in \(\mathrm{thm:all\mbox{-}regime\mbox{-}bracket}\).  For the upper inequality, put \(\ell=\log(ed)\).  Since \(d\geq2\), one has \(\ell=1+\log d>1\).  For every \(a\geq0\) and every \(\ell\geq1\),
\[
 \ell\min\!\left\{1,\frac a\ell\right\}=\min\{\ell,a\}\geq\min\{1,a\}.
\]
Taking \(a=d/n\) yields the first comparison requested in the claim:
\[
 U_{n,d}=\min\!\left(1,\frac dn\right)
 \leq \log(ed)\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
The first term in the maximum defining \(L_{n,d}\) in \(\mathrm{def:benchmarks}\) is exactly \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\).  Therefore
\[
 U_{n,d}
 \leq \log(ed)\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}
 \leq \log(ed)L_{n,d}.
\]
Combining this deterministic comparison with the upper inequality \(R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon U_{n,d}\) from \(\mathrm{thm:all\mbox{-}regime\mbox{-}bracket}\) proves
\[
 R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d}.
\]
The constants inherited from that theorem depend only on \(\epsilon\), which establishes uniformity.
added_lemmas.justification: This proposition turns the two explicit benchmark bounds into a same-class all-regime characterization whose only unresolved multiplicative loss is at most \(\log(ed)\).
added_lemmas.gap: The remaining logarithmic factor is not resolved by the existing lower families or the empirical estimator.
added_lemmas.consumer: The result gives a uniform quantitative approximation to the minimax risk before the exact sparse and transitional frontier is known.

added_lemmas.statement:
For every \(n>1\) and \(d\geq2\), the lower benchmark has the phase diagram
\[
L_{n,d}=
\begin{cases}
 d/n,
   & d\leq n^{1/3},\\
 n^{-2/3},
   & n^{1/3}<d\leq n^{1/3}\log(ed),\\
 d/[n\log(ed)],
   & n^{1/3}\log(ed)<d<n\log(ed),\\
 1,
   & d\geq n\log(ed).
\end{cases}
\]
At every shared boundary the adjacent formulas agree, so the displayed allocation of equality is immaterial.  The first branch condition \(d\leq n^{1/3}\) is equivalent to \(n\geq d^3\); on that branch \(\mathrm{thm:dense\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon L_{n,d}\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Fix \(n>1\) and \(d\geq2\), and abbreviate \(\ell=\log(ed)\).  Then \(\ell>1\).  By \(\mathrm{def:benchmarks}\),
\[
 L_{n,d}=\max\{A,B\},\qquad
 A=\min\!\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\ell}\right\},\qquad
 B=\min\!\left\{\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right\}.
\]
We evaluate this maximum in four exhaustive regimes.

If \(d\leq n^{1/3}\), then \(d/n\leq n^{-2/3}\), so \(B=d/n\).  Also \(\ell>1\) implies \(d/(n\ell)<d/n\leq1\), whence \(A=d/(n\ell)\leq B\).  Thus \(L_{n,d}=d/n\).

If \(n^{1/3}<d\leq n^{1/3}\ell\), then \(d/n>n^{-2/3}\), so \(B=n^{-2/3}\).  Moreover
\[
 \frac{d}{n\ell}\leq\frac{n^{1/3}\ell}{n\ell}=n^{-2/3}<1,
\]
where the last strict inequality uses \(n>1\).  Hence \(A=d/(n\ell)\leq B\), and \(L_{n,d}=n^{-2/3}\).

If \(n^{1/3}\ell<d<n\ell\), then \(d>n^{1/3}\), so \(B=n^{-2/3}\), while the upper inequality gives \(d/(n\ell)<1\), so \(A=d/(n\ell)\).  The lower inequality gives
\[
 A=\frac{d}{n\ell}>\frac{n^{1/3}\ell}{n\ell}=n^{-2/3}=B.
\]
Consequently \(L_{n,d}=d/[n\log(ed)]\).

Finally, if \(d\geq n\ell\), then \(d/(n\ell)\geq1\), so \(A=1\).  Since \(B\leq1\), it follows that \(L_{n,d}=1\).  These regimes are exhaustive because \(\ell>1\) and \(n>1\) imply
\[
 n^{1/3}<n^{1/3}\ell<n\ell.
\]
At \(d=n^{1/3}\), one has \(d/n=n^{-2/3}\); at \(d=n^{1/3}\ell\), one has \(d/(n\ell)=n^{-2/3}\); and at \(d=n\ell\), one has \(d/(n\ell)=1\).  Thus adjacent formulas coincide at all shared boundaries.

Because \(n,d>0\), cubing preserves order, and \(d\leq n^{1/3}\) is equivalent to \(d^3\leq n\).  On this first branch, \(L_{n,d}=d/n\) by the calculation above, while \(\mathrm{thm:dense\mbox{-}frontier}\) gives
\[
 c_\epsilon\frac dn\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}\leq C_\epsilon\frac dn.
\]
Substitution of \(L_{n,d}=d/n\) proves the final assertion.
added_lemmas.justification: The explicit branches expose every candidate elbow left for a sharp converse or improved estimator to confirm or remove.
added_lemmas.gap: Only the first branch is currently known to equal the minimax rate up to overlap-only constants.
added_lemmas.consumer: The phase diagram separates the proved dense frontier from the unresolved transitional and sparse regimes.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current wording treats the grouped handle too much like an already defined estimator and does not expose the newly proved at-most-logarithmic gap or its candidate elbows.  The replacement narrows the open task to closing that gap while requiring a genuinely explicit estimator and a matching converse on the unchanged model class.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed: This node is a candidate blueprint, not a constructed estimator.  A complete instantiation would have to specify, as deterministic functions of \(n\), \(d\), and \(\epsilon\), the sample split, pilot mass shells and effect intervals, degree \(K\), finite grid, joint four-cell factorial statistics, exact covariance bound, feasibility tolerances, nonnegative Hausdorff-moment program, aggregation and mass normalization, Rao--Blackwellization rule, and deterministic fallback.  Only after those choices are given and measurability, feasibility, and risk are proved does the resulting sample map define \(\widehat G_{\mathrm{grp}}\in\mathcal P([-1,1])\).
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The frozen construction is only a research recipe: it does not specify the split, tuning, factorial statistic, covariance control, optimization tolerances, or measurable fallback needed to define a sample map.  Its construction text must therefore identify it as a candidate blueprint rather than a delivered estimator.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Rename and reframe the incomplete grouped recipe as a candidate blueprint while retaining its inputs and notation.

proposed.justification: The remaining mathematical target is to remove the proved at-most-\(\log(ed)\) gap on the unchanged observational class and determine which candidate elbows are genuine.
proposed.gap: No verified argument yet controls the coupled mass-weighted treated--control moment process uniformly over the Lipschitz dual class, and the existing same-class lower families do not select the sharp interpolation.
proposed.consumer: A solved frontier would calibrate categorical-profile CATE-law reporting without asserting individual treatment-effect recovery or point identification of a zero atom.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Wire the restated open question to the proved logarithmic characterization and explicit phase diagram, and synchronize its framing with the fact that grouped reconstruction is only a candidate blueprint.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Remove the remaining at-most-\(\log(ed)\) factor, determine which displayed benchmark elbows are genuine, fully instantiate a measurable probability-valued grouped estimator, and prove a matching converse on the unchanged model class.
open_obligations.obstruction: Arbitrary unknown cell masses, null cells, tied effects, and unequal propensities at both overlap boundaries remain legal.  The deterministic mass-weighted Lipschitz extension does not control the supremum over all Lipschitz tests of the joint grouped factorial-moment error, while the scalar-transfer and separated-atom lower families certify different obstructions without determining their sharp interpolation.
open_obligations.attempted: The established route gives the total empirical upper bound, the normalized categorical scalar transfer, the separated-atom hypercube lower bound, and the exact dense frontier.  The algebraic comparison added here compresses these results to an at-most-logarithmic characterization and locates four candidate phases.  Summing cellwise errors recovers only the empirical upper benchmark; the candidate grouped blueprint still lacks a uniform covariance argument, optimized tuning, and a matching intermediate lower family.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The proved same-class characterization is
\[
 c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\leq R_{n,d,\epsilon}
 \leq C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d},
\]
where
\[
 L_{n,d}=\max\!\left\{
 \min\!\left(1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right),
 \min\!\left(\frac dn,n^{-2/3}\right)
 \right\}.
\]
For \(n>1\), its four branches are \(d/n\), \(n^{-2/3}\), \(d/[n\log(ed)]\), and \(1\), separated respectively by \(d=n^{1/3}\), \(d=n^{1/3}\log(ed)\), and \(d=n\log(ed)\).  The first branch is exactly the regime \(n\geq d^3\), where the same-class lower and empirical upper bounds match at order \(d/n\).  The empirical estimator continues to give the concrete bound \(C_\epsilon\min\{1,d/n\}\) on every two-effect-cluster subfamily with unknown unequal masses and propensities at either overlap boundary, without deleting null cells.  The existing bracket also yields the proved sufficient and necessary consistency conditions and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary, but it does not decide the exact consistency region or the genuine sparse and transitional elbows.

prose_updates.tldr: High-dimensional categorical adjustment makes every CATE location a difference of two armwise ratios, while the same unknown cell mass controls both sampling information and the atom's target weight.  On the unchanged observational model class, the paper proves the uniform logarithmic characterization \(c_\epsilon L_{n,d}\le R_{n,d,\epsilon}\le C_\epsilon\log(ed)L_{n,d}\), the exact \(d/n\) dense frontier when \(n\ge d^3\), and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary, using the explicit total empirical probability-valued estimator for achievability.  The exact sparse-to-dense frontier remains open: grouped reconstruction is an explicit candidate blueprint, not a delivered estimator, until its split, tuning, factorial statistics, covariance control, finite program, fallback, and matching same-class converse are supplied.

project_justification.fill: The paper supplies observed-law identification, a mass-weighted Lipschitz extension, a computable total empirical probability-valued estimator, complementary same-class lower constructions, a uniform at-most-\(\log(ed)\) characterization with an explicit four-branch lower-benchmark phase diagram, the exact \(d/n\) dense frontier, and the bounded-category parametric-risk boundary.  It also states an explicit grouped moment-reconstruction blueprint for attacking the remaining gap, without presenting that blueprint as a constructed or rate-certified estimator.

prose_updates.related_work: Zeng et al. use the same observed categorical model class with unknown masses, propensities, and arm regressions, but their target is a scalar mean rather than the population CATE law.  Vinayak--Kong--Kakade study a different paired-binomial experiment with common fixed trials and equal entity weights; Han--Jiao--Weissman study a different one-population multinomial experiment and local sorted-distribution moments; and Lee--Bacak--Kennedy work in a different heterogeneous-trial regularity regime with observed trial counts and smooth mixing densities.  These papers motivate approximation, positive reconstruction, and sparse-to-dense comparisons, but none supplies the coupled unknown-mass observational frontier here.  Kennedy et al. concern smooth CATE-function loss, Chernozhukov et al. motivate effect-distribution reporting under regular sorting, and Mizuguchi--Sawamura provide the categorical-profile dexamethasone application; none changes the present target or closes its remaining logarithmic gap.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier is not proved outside the dense branch: the current lower and upper bounds differ by at most \(\log(ed)\), and it is unknown which of the displayed \(n^{1/3}\), \(n^{1/3}\log(ed)\), and \(n\log(ed)\) elbows persist in the minimax rate.  The grouped reconstruction node is only a candidate blueprint.  It still requires an explicit split, shells, degree, grid, factorial statistic, exact covariance bound, feasibility tolerance, fallback, uniform Lipschitz-indexed risk proof, and matching same-class converse.  The early checks must retain unknown unequal weights, null cells, ties, and propensities at both overlap boundaries; a scalar-rate certificate contradicted by the separated-atom \(d/n\) floor must be rejected.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The target is the population law of conditional mean effects, not the law of individual potential-outcome differences, and Wasserstein recovery alone cannot certify an atom at zero.  What is proved is a same-class all-regime characterization within a factor of at most \(\log(ed)\), the exact \(d/n\) frontier for \(n\ge d^3\), the total empirical estimator's uniform risk bound, the stated one-sided consistency implications, and the exact bounded-category parametric-risk boundary.  The exact sparse and transitional rate, the exact consistency region, the genuineness of the candidate phase elbows, and any rate guarantee for the grouped blueprint remain open.

statement_notes.gap: The raw bracket is sharp in the dense branch but leaves an at-most-logarithmic factor in the sparse and transitional regimes.
statement_notes.consumer: The bounds provide valid sample-size diagnostics on the full observational class before the exact frontier is known.
